summary: Evan Thompson is a philosopher who studied at Amherst College under Robert A. F. Thurman and the University of Toronto, also working with Francisco Varela. His posts include York University (2002–2005), Toronto (2005), and the University of British Columbia (2013).

Eviatar Shulman works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem from ~1998 to 2008, where he also held posts in 2009, including department chairman in comparative religion.

Eyal Aviv works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and sinology. He earned his PhD at Harvard University (attested 2008) under Robert M. Gimello and Parimal G. Patil, and held a post at George Washington University in 2014.

F. B. J. Kuiper was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Utrecht under Willem Caland and Leiden under C. C. Uhlenbeck and Nicolaas van Wijk. He taught classics at Lyceum CAS (~1934–1939) and was professor of Sanskrit at Leiden (1939–1972).

Fa Qing works in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his dissertation at the University of Calgary, where he studied under Leslie S. Kawamura, Anthony W. Barber, and Ronald Neufeldt, among others.

Fabienne Jagou is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. She completed her PhD under Pierre-Étienne Will at the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences and held a post at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient (~2001).

Fabio Rambelli works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He studied at Ca' Foscari, Naples "L'Orientale", and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, later holding posts at Sapporo University (2001–2009) and the University of California, Santa Barbara (~2009).

Fabrizia Baldissera is an Indologist who studied at the Department of Mathematics "Federigo Enriques" (1969–2004). She has held posts at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" and the University of Florence.
Fafang was a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under Taixu. He held a post as a Research Fellow in Indian Buddhism at Visva-Bharati University.

Fang-Kuei Li was a linguist, sinologist, and tibetologist. He studied at Tsinghua, Michigan, and Chicago under Edward Sapir. He held positions at Academia Sinica, Yale, Harvard, the University of Washington (1949–1969), and the University of Hawaiʻi (1969–1974).
Faren works in Buddhist and religious studies. Faren earned a PhD from Lancaster University by 2008 and held a post as teaching consultant at The University of Hong Kong (attested 2013).

Farzand Ali Durrani was an archaeologist who studied at the University of Peshawar, the University of the Punjab, and the University of London (~1959–1964). He later served as a professor at the University of Peshawar (attested 1990).
Fausto Gherardo Fumi was an Italian scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at the Scuola Normale Superiore (~1858–1862) under Giuseppe Bardelli.

Fawad Khan is a scholar of archaeology and Buddhist studies. He earned a master's at the University of Peshawar and a PhD at Quaid-i-Azam University, later serving as Assistant Curator at Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's Directorate of Archaeology and Museums (attested 2022).

Fazun was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Wuchang Buddhist Institute under Taixu and at Drepung Monastery. He co-founded the Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Institute and held leadership roles at the Buddhist Academy of China (1956, 1980).

Ferdinand Christian Baur was a German scholar of religious studies and history. He studied at the University of Tübingen and the Tübinger Stift (~1809–1814) and later held a post at the University of Tübingen from ~1826 to 1860.

Ferdinand Hitzig was a scholar of religious studies and linguistics who studied under Heinrich Ewald (~1828–1829). He held academic posts at the University of Zurich (~1833–1861) and Heidelberg University (~1861–1875).

Ferdinand Justi was a scholar of Iranian/Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at Göttingen under Theodor Benfey and habilitated at Marburg, where he served as associate professor (1865), full professor (1869), and Rektor (1887–1888).

Ferdinand Lessing was a scholar of Tibetology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin. He held positions at Peking University (1919–1921), the Berlin Ethnological Museum (~1925–1935), and the University of California, Berkeley (~1935–1952).

Ferdinand Sommer was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate at Freiburg under Rudolf Thurneysen. He held professorships at Basel (1902), Rostock (1909–1913), Jena (1913–1924), Bonn (1924–1926), and Munich (1926–1951).
